clue.text: Make impossible claims at first in introduction

indicators.note: in places the opening letter of claims inside the word for an introduction

parts.note: a prelude is an introduction or opening piece

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word claims

explanation.surface: Someone's boastful claims made up front rule out a possibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to prevent it from happening, rendering it impossible.

clue.text: Get ready to paint, using mostly red and blue

indicators.note: mostly means the colour word loses its final letter

parts.note: ruby is a deep red colour
down means blue, as in feeling low

explanation.surface: A decorator prepares to paint a room chiefly in red and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' is the mood here, not a colour: DOWN means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub down a surface is to smooth it with sandpaper as preparation before painting.

clue.text: Ditch sermon that's bedevilled religious community

indicators.note: bedevilled means thrown into confusion, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A preacher throws away a sermon that has been causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DITCH and SERMON are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Christendom is the worldwide body of Christians, a religious community spanning nations.

clue.text: Trouble at college with scholastic group

parts.note: up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford
a set is a group of pupils of similar ability in a school

explanation.surface: Difficulties arise at a university involving a group of students.
explanation.walkthrough: Being UP at college is a British usage: you go up to university and come down at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to trouble or disturb them.

clue.text: Chosen artist for Greek tragedy

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president elect
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A selected painter is picked to stage an ancient drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a tragedy by Sophocles, and another by Euripides, about Agamemnon's daughter.

clue.text: Muse about an item found in the garage

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the name of the Muse is read backwards

parts.note: Clio is the Muse of history
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ponders a thing they come across among the tools in a garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder; it is the goddess CLIO, turned by 'about' to give OILC.
explanation.definitionFit: A can with a spout for oiling machinery is a typical piece of garage equipment.

clue.text: Where gymnast may be proceeding correctly

definitions.meaning: a gymnast performs on the balance beam
on course, following the guiding radio beam that keeps an aircraft on track

explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast balances on the beam, and an aircraft following its guidance beam is heading the right way.

clue.text: Pope born in July or August

definitions.meaning: several popes have taken this name, such as the thirteenth one of 1878
the zodiac sign of the lion covers late July to late August

explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen popes took the name, and the lion sign covers those born from late July to late August.

clue.text: A compound containing phosphorus and hydrogen that's produced when oil is distilled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: containing means the compound word holds the two element symbols inside it

parts.note: salt is a chemical compound
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about a substance made from phosphorus and hydrogen during refining.
explanation.definitionFit: This black tarry substance is left as a residue in the distillation of crude petroleum.

clue.text: Chinese delicacy that's taken home for young family

definitions.meaning: a prized dish of China made from swiftlet saliva nests
a nest is the home of a brood of chicks, here taken and eaten as a dish

explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese dish is made from swiftlet nests, literally the homes where chicks are raised.

clue.text: Track, it may be announced, for fat controller?

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a track is a course, followed by the word it

explanation.surface: A railway announcement about a line, with a nod to a famous stout railway boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat Controller' recalls the portly railway boss in the Thomas the Tank Engine stories, keeping the track theme; here it is a garment that controls fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight undergarment is worn to hold in and shape the waist, controlling a fleshy figure.

clue.text: Attlee worried about leaders of the opposition abstaining

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the two opening letters
worried means agitated, so the name's letters are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leaders of asks for the first letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: A postwar Labour prime minister frets about Tory chiefs refusing something.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was a British Labour prime minister; 'the opposition' suggests his Tory rivals, but only its first letters are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains completely from alcohol is described as teetotal.

clue.text: Break knocker?

definitions.meaning: a break is a lucky chance, as in a big break
proverbially, this is what knocks only once

explanation.definitionFit: A lucky break is a chance, and the saying holds that a chance knocks only once.

clue.text: Lacking will to accept right road

indicators.note: to accept means the phrase takes the letter in among its own letters

parts.note: intestate means dying without having made a will

explanation.surface: A man without a valid will is ready to accept the proper way forward.
explanation.definitionFit: In the United States a highway running between states is called an interstate.

clue.text: Lawman's first to stop one unknown killer

indicators.note: to stop means plug a gap, so the letter goes inside the word for a person unknown

parts.note: a stranger is someone unknown to you

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word Lawman's

explanation.surface: A sheriff is the first to halt a mysterious murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one unknown' looks like algebra's X or Y, but it is a STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a murderer who kills by choking the victim.

clue.text: Kick rejected earthenware here

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: to kick a habit is to stop it

explanation.surface: A potter angrily kicks unwanted crockery around the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick' is not a foot's blow but giving up, as in kicking a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots are vessels made of fired clay, typical earthenware items.

clue.text: Poet not admitted for audition

indicators.note: audition here means hearing, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: barred means kept out or refused entry

explanation.surface: A poet is turned away when trying out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' suggests a casting call, but it means hearing: BARRED said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, especially one in the old minstrel tradition.

clue.text: Paint short girl eating blubber

indicators.note: eating means the shortened name surrounds the other word
short means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
to blubber is to cry noisily

explanation.surface: A small girl munching whale fat, oddly with paint about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like whale fat but is the verb, weeping: CRY. 'short' trims ALICE to ALIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a quick-drying synthetic paint used by artists and decorators.

clue.text: Cockney's Indian singer

definitions.meaning: in rhyming slang the singer's name stands for a curry, an Indian meal
a Northern Irish popular singer of the 1950s

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes with it; 'an Indian' is a curry in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belfast-born vocalist's name became rhyming slang for a curry, the dish Britons call an Indian.

clue.text: Weapon carrier without locks, not fully loaded

parts.note: locks are hair, so without them is bald

indicators.note: not fully means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: loaded is slang for rich

explanation.surface: A gun carrier with a shaved head whose weapon is not fully charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' suggests a gun but means wealthy: RICH, cut to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt worn over the shoulder to carry a sword.

clue.text: 7, say, going topless in river where bridge is noted

indicators.note: in places the trimmed word inside the river's name

parts.note: the Avon is an English river

indicators.note: going topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the answer to 7-down is an example of a zodiac sign

explanation.surface: A topless bather wades into a river at a spot known for its bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' hints at the song Sur le Pont d'Avignon, about the city's famous bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: This French city is famous for its medieval bridge, celebrated in a well-known children's song.

clue.text: Mafioso, possibly from Italian city, almost captured in US state

indicators.note: captured in means the shortened city goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California

indicators.note: almost means the city's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Rimini is a resort city on Italy's Adriatic coast

explanation.surface: A mobster from Italy is nearly caught in California.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Mafia is an example of a lawbreaker, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Beautiful young women call American novelist

parts.note: ho is a call to attract attention, as in land ho
Leon Uris was the American author of Exodus

explanation.surface: Lovely girls telephone a writer from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' suggests a phone call, but it is the cry HO.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic belief, houris are beautiful maidens of paradise; the word now means alluring young women.

clue.text: Washed tights beginning to dry

parts.note: hose is an old word for tights or stockings

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of the word dry

explanation.surface: Laundered tights are just starting to dry on the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To hose something is to wash it down with water from a hose.

clue.text: Ukrainian formerly suffering Stalinist rule

indicators.note: suffering means damaged or distressed, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A citizen of Ukraine in the past endured harsh Soviet dictatorship.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of STALINIST RULE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Russian was an old, now offensive, name for a Ukrainian under the Russian Empire.

clue.text: Shoddy items whichever way you look in tourist attraction

indicators.note: in signals letters found within the two words, and whichever way you look says they read the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A tourist spot full of cheap tat wherever you turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'tourist' and the start of 'attraction', and reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods, such as souvenir junk.

clue.text: 10's dicky bird

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 10-across, a tight undergarment

explanation.surface: A dicky bird refers to a little bird, and 10 is the cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky bird' is a childish phrase for a small bird, but 'dicky' (unsound) is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts.

clue.text: Stinker failing coursework?

parts.note: a cad is a rotter or stinker, a dishonourable man
dying means failing or fading away

explanation.surface: A rotter flunking his school assignments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coursework' suggests school; here it is work on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying a golfer's clubs round the links is literally work done on a golf course.
